title: Reverse a Short Function to C — 2026-09-07 (Windows x86-64)
blurb:
Challenge: Reverse this Windows x64 function (int n in ecx, result in eax) to equivalent C:

sum_digits:
    xor   r9d, r9d
.loop:
    test  ecx, ecx
    jz    .done
    mov   eax, ecx
    cdq
    mov   r8d, 10
    idiv  r8d
    add   r9d, edx
    mov   ecx, eax
    jmp   .loop
.done:
    mov   eax, r9d
    ret

Answer: int sum_digits(int n) { int sum = 0; while (n != 0) { int q = n / 10; int r = n % 10; sum += r; n = q; } return sum; } -- cdq sign-extends ecx into edx:eax so idiv r8d does signed division by 10, leaving quotient in eax and remainder in edx; each pass adds the remainder (least-significant decimal digit) to r9d and feeds the quotient back into ecx; test/jz is the zero-test loop guard, so the loop sums one decimal digit of n per iteration.
